part: Mobile 390 — the nav drawer, opened (288px, scrim, header block, 44px rows, one-row footer)
artboards: mobile-390 text spec, DRAWER section (no artboard PNG exists yet)
source: docs/design/handoff-2026-09-06/DEVIATION-LOG.md 'MOBILE 390 SPEC', DRAWER section. No artboard PNG for 390 has reached the repo; the text spec is the binding source until one does, and when one arrives the image wins and the differences are logged.
notes: The drawer's measures only exist while it is open, and AppShell owns that state (the hamburger opens it, never a prop). The `mobile-drawer` mount renders the SAME AppShell + DashboardBrief tree as `page-frame-1440` and clicks the real hamburger, so what is measured here is the drawer a reader actually opens — no test-only prop was added to product code.

FOOTER: the mobile 390 spec's DRAWER section still describes 'two unlabelled 44px rows: Account with the workspace name, Admin with the OWNER badge'. That wording is SUPERSEDED by the operator's 2026-09-07 third-set ruling ('we dont need seperate account and admin buttons visable if they pop up as options when you clicked on the logged in person name there'), which makes the footer ONE row — the logged-in person's name with the workspace name right-aligned, opening the menu that holds Workspace profile, Admin panel, Settings and Sign out. The later ruling wins over the earlier text spec; this file asserts the one row, and the difference is logged in DEVIATION-LOG.md.

Section labels and counts are the same SECTIONS table the desktop nav card uses (one table, two size variants inside Sidebar's own row builder), so they are not re-asserted here beyond the label's own type.

Row counts are not asserted here: they come from the workspace-bootstrap fetch, which this mount answers with nothing, so no count span renders. The count itself is one branch of the SAME renderNavItem builder the desktop card uses (11px on the drawer variant, --fs-11 on the card), and the card's is measured by sidebar.json.
